baseline_models.focus_anchor: The restrictive construction fa-innama hiya predicates zajratun wahidatun: a sound-based zajrah explicitly counted as one.
baseline_models.mechanism: A vocal rebuke or driving call is packaged as one bounded impulse; its sound is not commentary on the action but the means by which restraint or motion is effected.

activation_trace.role: Sound-based rebuke, restraint, expulsion, or urging supplies an acoustic act that can directly alter its addressee's motion.
The numerical one bounds the effective acoustic act as a single count.

changed_reading.before: A rebuke or cry happens once.
changed_reading.after: One bounded vocal command is sufficient, with the sound itself functioning as the restraining or propelling act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Zajrah can drive a recipient, while wahidah can describe things brought under one direction or judgment.
baseline_models.mechanism: The singularity is qualitative as well as numerical: one control signal can align a plurality into a common trajectory or state.

activation_trace.role: The driving function of a voiced zajrah supplies directional control over responsive recipients.
Union in one direction, connection, or judgment turns 'one' into convergence rather than bare counting.

changed_reading.before: The verse isolates one cry from any others.
changed_reading.after: The verse presents a single coordinating signal that can make many recipients move or stand under one disposition.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The restrictive fa-innama hiya construction can foreground the one zajrah, and the focus inventory permits wahidah to mark lack of peer.
baseline_models.mechanism: The cry's oneness may mark non-substitutability: its efficacy belongs to an utterance without an equal, not merely to the first unit in a countable series.

activation_trace.role: The voiced command provides the utterance whose authority is being characterized.
Being without peer or analogue supplies a qualitative reading of the utterance's singularity.

changed_reading.before: Wahidah reports only that the cry is numerically one.
changed_reading.after: Wahidah can also color the cry as unmatched in efficacy, while the numerical reading remains live.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening sequence supplies release, movement, precedence, management, and command as linked operations. Against it, the focus zajrah reads as a compact dispatch signal that initiates and coordinates a differentiated action-chain into one execution.

activation_trace.role: A voiced urging or restraining act supplies the initiating control signal.
Convergence in one direction supplies the common execution state reached by varied operations.
A loop or knot being tied and released supplies an enabling release stage.
Running or swimming supplies sustained movement after release.
Advancing and racing supplies ordered precedence within the moving process.
Managing an affair by attending to its outcome supplies coordination of the sequence.
Request and obligation supply the executable-command character of the managed affair.

structural_cues: 79:1-5 forms an ordered series of intensive action phrases, with fa-transitions into precedence and management.
The opening series ends in management of an amr before the disturbance and return sequence begins.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered operations and a managed command; the reader supplies the arrow from the focus cry to their coordinated execution. A live alternative is that the opening agents act independently and merely establish capacity rather than a dispatch mechanism for 79:13.

changed_reading.before: One isolated cry acts directly on an unspecified recipient.
changed_reading.after: One dispatch can release, set in motion, order, and coordinate a multi-stage operation as a unified execution.

context_deltas.mechanism: Severe disturbance and explicit return/repetition language surround the focus clause, but its one zajrah is followed by an immediate new state. Thus 'one' measures the sufficiency of the transition-trigger, not the total number of motions or stages in the surrounding sequence.

activation_trace.role: The sound that makes its object recoil or move supplies the operative transition impulse.
Numerical oneness marks a single sufficient impulse within a larger sequence.
Severe disturbance supplies the unstable pre-transition field.
Return or restoration to a place supplies the disputed reversal that the cry effects.
Return and repetition after a prior time supplies the recurrence the speakers deem disastrous.

structural_cues: 79:6-7 explicitly stages one disturbance followed by another, so wahidah in 79:13 cannot flatten every surrounding event into one.
The restrictive nominal clause of 79:13 answers the skeptical return speech and is followed by fa-idha in 79:14, marking an abrupt realized state.
79:14 supplies the branchless س ه ر occurrence as the immediate post-cry state, so it is used structurally rather than branch-cited.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies serial disturbance, disputed recurrence, and an immediate post-cry state; the reader infers that the cry operationalizes the phase change and that oneness marks sufficiency. A live alternative is that the verse simply counts one conventional blast without emphasizing threshold mechanics.

changed_reading.before: The one cry is merely another item in an eschatological sequence.
changed_reading.after: The one cry is the decisive hinge whose single occurrence is enough to convert contested return into an accomplished state.

context_deltas.mechanism: The Musa-Pharaoh sequence stages a divine call, a ruler's gathering call, a sovereignty claim, and an exemplary deterrent. It activates the focus cry as an unmatched counter-sovereign utterance: one authoritative voice gathers and restrains more effectively than a claimant's mass proclamation.

activation_trace.role: A forceful voiced rebuke supplies the authoritative counter-command.
Lack of peer supplies the command's unmatched authority rather than only its count.
Raising the voice in a call supplies the commissioning voice that begins the confrontation.
Driving and collecting a group toward a destination supplies the social reach sought by Pharaoh's call.
The raised public call supplies the rival voice whose authority is tested.
Lordship, possession, and sovereignty identify what the public utterance claims.
Greatness and domineering arrogance sharpen the rival claim to supreme voice.
Punishment that restrains others turns the answer to false sovereignty into exemplary deterrence.

structural_cues: 79:16 and 79:23 repeat calling on opposite sides of the confrontation.
79:23-25 moves from gathering and proclamation through a supreme lordship claim to divine seizure and deterrent consequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies competing calls, gathered listeners, a sovereignty claim, and deterrent punishment; the reader treats them as a contest of effective voices and maps the focus cry to the decisive counter-voice. A live alternative is that the narrative demonstrates power generally without specifying a vocal contest behind 79:13.

changed_reading.before: The cry is an impersonal eschatological sound.
changed_reading.after: The cry can be heard as the single unmatched command that ends rival claims to commanding voice and converts proclamation into judgment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later fork between transgression and refuge contains an exact restraint image: the self is checked from its inclination, while warning awakens caution. This gives the external zajrah an internal ethical analogue, a decisive inhibitory command that redirects a living self before the final command redirects all recipients.

activation_trace.role: Restraint and prevention within the voiced zajrah supply the external form of inhibition.
Bringing things under one direction supplies the redirected trajectory produced by restraint.
Rebuke and checking from an act provide a direct internal echo of the focus root's restraining function.
The thing's own self or identity supplies the recipient and locus of self-restraint.
The self's desire and inclination supply the trajectory that inhibition interrupts.
A warning that frightens and awakens caution supplies the pre-event voice capable of eliciting restraint.

structural_cues: 79:37-41 forms a two-outcome fork between transgressive preference and fearful self-restraint.
79:40 gives restraint an explicit object and blocked direction, while 79:45 closes the surah's address with the role of warning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact restraint branch, a self, its inclination, and an awakening warning; the reader supplies an analogy between ethical inhibition now and the final external zajrah. A live alternative is that this is only thematic echo and that the two restraints should not be identified as the same event.

changed_reading.before: The zajrah belongs only to a future external event.
changed_reading.after: The future cry also exposes a present pattern of effective command: a warning can become an inward check that turns the self away from its prior inclination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing questions seek the hour's anchorage and endpoint, then retrospectively compress worldly duration to an evening or morning. The one zajrah therefore functions as an indivisible temporal boundary: it terminates an extended interval and makes the former duration contract from the far side of the transition.

activation_trace.role: The bounded vocal act supplies the event that crosses and enforces the temporal boundary.
Separation and standing apart supply the cry's role as a discrete boundary between temporal regimes.
Fixity and rooted stability supply the sought anchoring of the terminal hour.
The limit at which a thing ends supplies the hour's terminal boundary.
A duration of time supplies the interval whose experienced scale is reassessed.
Remaining in a place supplies the apparently long stay that contracts retrospectively.
Evening time supplies one short measure used for the compressed stay.
The morning's extension supplies the alternate short measure of that compressed stay.

structural_cues: 79:42 asks when the hour will be anchored, 79:44 assigns its endpoint, and 79:46 shifts to retrospective duration.
The final simile offers evening and morning as alternatives, making temporal rescaling rather than an exact elapsed measurement salient.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies anchorage, endpoint, duration, and its retrospective compression; the reader supplies the arrow by which the single cry creates the boundary that causes this rescaling. A live alternative is that the cry and the final duration simile are separate effects of the hour rather than one temporal mechanism.

changed_reading.before: One describes only the short count of the cry.
changed_reading.after: The one cry is an indivisible terminal boundary whose completion makes an extended former life appear no longer than part of a day.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it imports pastoral mechanics into an eschatological noun. It remains anchored because the focus branch explicitly includes driving animals or clouds by sound, while the context supplies pasture, cattle, and a branch in which a call settles a herd. Downstream prose should mark it only as a material analogy ('can be heard as'), not as lexical disambiguation or a replacement for the rebuke-command reading.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Focus z-j-r B001 includes urging or checking animals and clouds by sound, and focus w-h-d B005 permits many recipients to be brought into one direction.

activation_trace.role: Driving animals or clouds by a voiced call supplies the pastoral acoustic mechanism anchored in zajrah itself.
Union in one direction supplies the gathered trajectory of the responsive multitude.
Grazing and pasture supply the material field of herd movement.
Livestock wealth, especially camels, supplies the responsive herd image.
A herd settling at a male's call supplies a packet-internal analogue for acoustic control producing collective rest.

changed_reading.before: The one cry is pictured only as a punitive blast.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it can be pictured as one cosmic herding call by which dispersed life is driven and settled into a single destination.

strongest_changes: The surrounding sequence turns a counted cry into one sufficient phase-transition trigger amid multiple preceding motions.
The opening operations recast the cry as a unified dispatch capable of coordinating release, movement, precedence, and management.
The exact restraint echo in 79:40 gives the final external command a distinct internal ethical analogue without requiring the two events to be identical.
The closing anchorage and duration language makes the cry an indivisible temporal boundary, not merely a short sound.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly couples voice with control: operational command, return, rival proclamation, deterrence, self-restraint, and temporal finality. This allowed numerical, directional, sovereign, ethical, and boundary readings of the same tightly anchored focus construction to coexist.
remaining_uncertainties: Wahidah may chiefly count one cry; its directional-unity, boundary, and unmatched-efficacy branches remain secondary activations.
The dispatch reading depends on an analogical causal link from 79:1-5 to 79:13 rather than an explicit syntactic link.
The internal-restraint and pastoral readings should remain qualified analogies, not identifications of the focus event.
